fields.explore_cta: Build My Pest Control Landing Page
fields.features_heading: The Parts That Turn a Sighting Into a Booking
fields.features_subheading: A pest control landing page has one job: getting an inspection or treatment request. Emergent builds each part below from a prompt.
fields.feature_1:
The pest, picked from a short list

Open the form with fixed choices: Ants, Mice or rats, Termites, Wasps, and Bed bugs. The pick decides which technician hears about the request and what the form asks next.
fields.feature_2:
Inspection or treatment, asked once

Ask whether the visitor wants an inspection first or a treatment on the calendar. Inspection requests go to the inspector's list, and treatments go to whoever plans routes.
fields.feature_3:
Home or business before the address

Ask the property type next: Home, Rental, Restaurant, or Warehouse. A business answer then opens questions a home never sees, such as how many locations the business has.
fields.feature_4:
Every request saved where you can sort it

Each request lands in a database you own with the pest, the property type, the address, and the time it came in. The office marks the row Booked once it is on a route.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts to the inspector or the office

Send termite requests to the inspector by email and the rest to an office Slack channel, or to both. Each alert carries the visitor's phone number and the pest they picked.
fields.feature_6:
Code your developer can pick up

Paid plans export the full code of the page to your GitHub repository, where a developer can keep working in the same files. Until then, Emergent changes the page by prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
Mud tubes and soft wood reach the inspector

Copperfen Pest Solutions opens its termite form on one question: what have you seen? Mud tubes or Soft wood sends the request to Ruthanne Nkemdi, the termite inspector. A visitor who picks Not sure gets a call from the office first. This month 31 termite requests came in: 22 went to Ruthanne and 9 picked Not sure.
fields.tab_content_2:
Plan prices by home size, before anyone calls

Sallowmere Pest Co. sells a quarterly plan and shows the price as soon as the visitor picks a home size: $129 a visit under 2,500 sq ft, or $149 a visit at 2,500 sq ft and up. The size and the price are already on the row when the office calls back. Of 40 plan requests this month, 28 were under 2,500 sq ft and 12 were larger.
fields.tab_content_3:
Nests by a door go out the same day

Brindlemoor Pest Control asks one thing first on its nest page: where is the nest? A nest marked By a door sends an email to Tavish Orme, the technician on same-day calls, and every other nest goes on Thursday's route. On Tuesday morning 9 nest requests came in: 6 were by a door and 3 went to Thursday.
fields.tab_content_4:
Restaurants on 3 or more sites go to Wendeline

Pellam Street Pest Services gives restaurants their own page, which asks how many locations the business runs. A restaurant on 3 or more sites goes to Wendeline Ostby, who manages chains. A single site goes to the commercial desk. This quarter 14 restaurants sent a request: 5 went to Wendeline and 9 to the desk.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Pest Control Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to build a pest control landing page that routes every inspection and treatment request to the right person.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask what the visitor has seen
fields.howto_step_1_des: Point a termite ad at an inspection page and a seasonal offer at a treatment page. A homeowner who found mud tubes wants an inspector, not a price list, and each page keeps one button for its one request.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Make the first field a short list of what the visitor found, such as Mud tubes or A nest, instead of an open text box. That answer picks who hears about the request. Put it ahead of the name and the phone number.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Show the pests you handle as choices, and add Other with a short text box. A visitor whose pest is not on the list can still send a request, and the office reads what it is before calling back.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask whether the request is for a home or a business. A business answer can open extra questions that a homeowner never sees, such as the number of locations or the hours the site is closed to customers.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide who hears about each request
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one line per route in your prompt, such as nests by a door to the same-day technician and every other request to the office list. Emergent builds the routing from those lines and changes it when you prompt again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Show the price where you can
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the price on the page for any service sold at a fixed price, such as a quarterly plan priced by home size. Leave it off inspections that need a visit first, and say on the page that the inspector quotes after looking.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form once for each route before the page goes live. Check that each test lands in the database as its own row, and that the alert reaches the right person with the phone number in it.

faq_plan.q: What is a pest control landing page?
faq_plan.a: A pest control landing page is a single page that turns a visitor from an ad, a mailer, or a search into an inspection or treatment request. It asks what the visitor has seen and how to reach them, and it has one button for that one request.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a pest control landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder: the pests you treat, the question to ask first, and who should hear about each request. Emergent builds the page, its form, and the database from that prompt. Send a test request, change anything by prompting again, then publish.

faq_plan.q: What should a pest control landing page ask first?
faq_plan.a: Ask which pest the visitor has, or what they have seen, as one tap on a short list. Keep Not sure on that list. A visitor who cannot name the pest still sends the request, and the office calls to ask.

faq_plan.q: Should inspections and treatments get separate pest control landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you sell both. An inspection request needs an inspector and a visit, while a treatment request may need a price and a route day. Separate pages let each ad land on the page for its own request. The same split helps on a roofing landing page, where an inspection and a repair quote are different requests.

faq_plan.q: Should a pest control landing page show prices?
faq_plan.a: Yes, where the price is set before anyone visits. Put it next to the button, and the office call starts with a date instead of a quote. Work that needs an inspection gets a line saying the inspector prices it on site.

faq_plan.q: How does a pest control landing page send requests to the right technician?
faq_plan.a: Route on answers the form already collects: the pest, the property type, or where a nest is. Write each rule in your prompt, such as termite sightings to the inspector and everything else to the office. The app Emergent builds sends email or Slack alerts, with the visitor's phone number in each one.

faq_plan.q: How should a pest control landing page handle urgent requests?
faq_plan.a: Add one question that marks a request as urgent, such as whether a nest is by a door, and send those requests to the technician on same-day calls. Everything else waits for the next route day. An HVAC landing page sorts no-heat calls from routine ones in the same way.

faq_plan.q: What should a pest control landing page for restaurants ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask the number of locations and the hours each site is closed to customers. A chain can then go to an account manager and a single site to the commercial desk. The app Emergent builds keeps each request, with its location count, in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a pest control landing page show after a request is sent?
faq_plan.a: Show who will call back and by when, such as the office within one business day, and repeat the phone number for anyone who cannot wait. If the visitor picked a time, put it on the confirmation. Keep the next step on that screen, not in a later email.

faq_plan.q: What makes a pest control landing page trustworthy to homeowners?
faq_plan.a: Proof a homeowner can check: photos of your own technicians and trucks, and reviews that name the pest and the neighborhood. List the towns you serve near the form. A contractor landing page leans on the same kind of proof, with photos of finished jobs.

plan.angle: The top 10 for pest control landing page is design galleries (Dribbble, Behance, Pinterest, a vector stock set), two example roundups, one lead-generation blog and one inspection template: they show how a pest control page looks, never what happens to an inspection or treatment request once it is sent. This page shows four pest control landing pages built around the request itself (a termite inspection request routed by what the homeowner saw, a quarterly plan price shown by home size, a wasp nest request near a door sent to a technician the same day, a restaurant page that sorts chains from single sites), each with the form, the routing and the database row behind it, then gives the build steps. It makes no pesticide, safety, health or licensing claims and nothing state-specific. HVAC, plumber, roofing and contractor pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Pest Control Landing Page for Inspections and Treatments'; hero 'Build a pest control landing page that books inspections and treatments, with every request kept in a database you own.'

intent.evidence: Top 10 are example and template galleries; page delivers four worked examples (Copperfen termite, Sallowmere quarterly plan, Brindlemoor wasp nests, Pellam Street restaurants), a 7-step how-to and a comparison table.

specificity.evidence: 'Mud tubes or Soft wood sends the request to Ruthanne Nkemdi, the termite inspector'; 'Home, Rental, Restaurant, or Warehouse'; 'every other nest goes on Thursday's route'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence, e.g. 'Copperfen Pest Solutions opens its termite form on one question: what have you seen?'

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; QC Q9 flags 'request' 18 times outside the FAQ (noted).

voice.evidence: Calm, product-led: 'The office marks the row Booked once it is on a route.'

truth.evidence: claims_used prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, code-export all in rules/capabilities.json; no pesticide-safety, health, licensing or state-law claim anywhere; numbers add up (22+9=31, 28+12=40, 6+3=9, 5+9=14).

distinct.evidence: Pest-specific routing (sighting, nest location, home size pricing, restaurant chains); hvac, roofing, contractor appear only as FAQ link sentences, never as headings or targets.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, each answered in its first sentence, e.g. 'Should a pest control landing page show prices? Yes, where the price is set before anyone visits.'
